system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: As of August 2026, where a Thai government agency or state enterprise engages an individual under a service-hire arrangement, what holiday and leave rights must it provide, and which court has jurisdiction over disputes? Answer briefly, covering both points.
raw_response:
Under the Thai Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998), as amended, individuals engaged under a service-hire arrangement by a Thai government agency or state enterprise are entitled to paid annual leave and public holidays as prescribed in Section 37 and Section 38, respectively. Specifically, they are entitled to at least 6 days of paid annual leave per year after one year of continuous service, and paid public holidays as defined by the government.

Disputes arising from such arrangements fall under the jurisdiction of the Labour Relations Board (LRB) and, if unresolved, may be appealed to the Labour Court, as provided under Section 10 of the Labour Relations Act B.E. 2518 (1975).
